> the result. The frozen development result is in `../SUMMARY.md`; the
> full 2016-2026 audit, the post-tune variants and the research-validity

# Close-Flow Exhaustion — `intraday-seasonality` (revisit)

**Status: design frozen, test pending. `result.json` deliberately absent.**
Backtests were paused by the lead on 2026-11-26 before this design was run.

## 1. The idea extracted from the original

The original `agents2/intraday-seasonality` was the round-1 winner with a
30-minute overlay: on a risk-on day where QQQ was more than 1% below its 09:30
open at 15:00, it sold TQQQ at the 15:01 open and bought back at 15:30.

The shared 165-day QQQ SMA supplied the entire book — when to own TQQQ, how much
crash protection to carry, and what to do in a bear market. The overlay only
removed 30 minutes. The genuinely new content was therefore a single claim about
the close:

> On a down day, part of the late selling is mechanical: daily-reset leveraged
> ETFs must reduce exposure in the direction of the day's move, and they do it in
> the close. The closing print is temporarily too cheap.

## 2. Standalone hypothesis

The standalone form of that claim is **not** "hold TQQQ and step aside for 30
minutes". It is:

> **Own TQQQ only for the reversal window.** Buy the closing print on an orderly,
> intraday-led QQQ decline, hold one session, and sit in BIL the rest of the time.

The signal now decides *when to be long at all* (about 11% of sessions), not when
to trim a permanent long. Universe, entry time, holding period, sizing and risk
all follow from the flow idea rather than from the old base.

### Why this is not just the old overlay minus the gate

| | original | rebuild |
|---|---|---|
| exposure | ~99% of bars | ~11% of bars |
| holding period | removes 30 minutes | owns a 23-hour reversal |
| position logic | long by default, de-risk on weakness | flat by default, long only after weakness |
| base | 165-day SMA + 4% stop | none |
| return driver | trend beta + crash avoidance | close-flow reversal |

The earlier attempt to keep the "de-risk" direction without the gate failed on
its own terms: a long-TQQQ book with the carve but **no** gate still correlates
**0.71** with the 165-day baseline (dev, pre-pause). Any always-in equity book
will, because both are driven by the same TQQQ beta. Only a part-time book can
pass the correlation rule, and the part-time version of the idea is the
reversal entry.

## 3. Universe, data and costs

- Tradeable: **TQQQ** long, **BIL** cash. Long-only, one position, ≤ 100%.
- Signal: **QQQ** 1-minute bars.
- Local adjusted 1-minute archive, 2016-01-04 → 2026-10-23, regular session.
- SPY daily is a benchmark only.
- Fills: next-bar open, 2% band, `research/bt.py`. 1 bp headline, 5/10 bp
  reported. 1-minute equity marks.
- No new data was needed, so nothing was added under `data/round3/`.

## 4. Exact rules

```
For each session d:
  at the 15:58 bar close (15:58:59 ET):
      q_day = QQQ(15:58) / QQQ(09:30 open) - 1
      if q_day <= -1.0%:  target = 100% TQQQ, filled at the 15:59 open
      else:               target = 100% BIL

  if long: sell at the next session's 15:01 open (one-session hold)
```

- Nothing after 15:58:59 is used for the decision.
- Early-close sessions (18 in the sample) never fire, because they lack a 15:58
  bar. If the *exit* session is an early close, the position is sold at the next
  session's open — the earliest executable price.
- No moving average anywhere in the position logic.
- If a new signal fires on the exit day, the book re-enters at that day's 15:59;
  back-to-back events are allowed and each pays its own round trip.

### Sizing and risk

- Base: 100% of equity when active, 0% otherwise. No leverage beyond TQQQ's own 3x.
- No stop in the base spec: the position is one session old and the exit is fixed.
- Pre-registered risk variants: a −5% close-based stop, a crash bound
  (`q_day >= -2.5%`), and a gap filter (`|gap| <= 0.5%`).

## 5. Pre-registered tests and variants

Full grid in `SPEC.md`. Summary:

| id | change | values |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | threshold | −0.75, **−1.0**, −1.25, −1.5% |
| V2 | crash bound | none, −2.5, −3.0% |
| V3 | gap filter | none, 0.5% |
| V4 | entry | **15:59**, 15:30 |
| V5 | exit | **next 15:00**, next open |
| V6 | stop | **none**, −5% |
| V7 | hold | **1**, 2 sessions |
| V8 | sizing | **full**, scaled by `|q_day|/2%` |

Bold = base spec, fixed before any test. 768 combinations; parameters must be
chosen from a plateau, not the best cell.

Placebos: same trade after **up** days (P1), on **random** sessions (P2), on
**shuffled** dates within year (P3), and selected on the **gap** instead of the
intraday move (P4) to measure overlap with the gap-reversal rebuild.

## 6. Preliminary evidence (pre-pause, not a result)

One development-only exploration was run before the pause
(`explore_dev.py`, 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29, 1 bp, no holdout data loaded).
It tested the naive version (entry 15:31, exit next 15:01, threshold −1%, no
filters):

| variant | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | exposure | corr vs 165d |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| long TQQQ always | 36.4% | 82.3% | 0.80 | 100% | 0.71 |
| long TQQQ + 15:00-15:30 carve on weak days | 41.0% | 79.8% | 0.85 | 99% | 0.71 |
| **buy 15:30 after QQQ < −1%, hold to next 15:00** | **19.4%** | **43.4%** | **0.69** | **10.9%** | **0.25** |
| buy 15:30, hold only to next open | 1.0% | 44.5% | 0.17 | 0.9% | 0.19 |

Sub-periods of the 19.4% version: 2016-19 13.7% CAGR / 21.4% DD / 0.67;
2020-21 44.3% / 43.4% / 1.02; 2022-23 8.7% / 36.2% / 0.41.

Caveats: this used a 15:31 entry (not the close), no crash filter, no stop, and a
single threshold. It is the reason to test the idea, not proof of it. The
baseline for the correlation is the shared 165-day book; it is computed only as a
metric and is never a position in this strategy.

## 7. Expected correlation and collision risk

- **vs the 165-day baseline: ~0.20-0.30** (measured 0.25 on the pre-pause
  version). The book is invested ~11% of bars, in one-session bursts.
- **vs `gap-capitulation-reversal`: 0.4-0.6 expected.** Different trigger
  (intraday move vs opening gap) and entry (15:59 vs open), but the same broad
  "buy after a decline" family. Must be measured; if > 0.70, this strategy
  yields, because the gap version is the cleaner expression of that mandate.
- **vs `letf-rebalance-flow`: expected low.** That strategy owns the flow signal;
  this one is a long-only reversal book.
- **vs `time-of-day`: expected ~0.3.** That one is an overnight book; this one
  only incidentally spans a night.

## 8. Falsifiers

- **F1** Dev 1 bp: CAGR < 6.0% or Sharpe < 0.50.
- **F2** Correlation vs the 165-day baseline > 0.60.
- **F3** Mean return per event at 5 bp ≤ 0.
- **F4** Any dev sub-period has negative CAGR.
- **F5** The up-day placebo matches or beats the down-day signal on Sharpe.
- **F6** Fewer than 150 dev events and bootstrap p ≥ 0.05.
- **F7** With the gap filter on the edge vanishes and the base is dominated by
  gap-down days → the idea is gap-capitulation, not close flow; retire.

## 9. Results

**PENDING — not run.** Backtests are paused. When authorised, the lead runs:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\27175\Desktop\quant-trader-research
$env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\Users\27175\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\pylibs"
python research\revisit\intraday-seasonality\strategy.py --windows dev
```

and, once frozen and audited, the holdout exactly once.

Placeholders to fill:

| window | 1 bp CAGR / DD / Sharpe | 5 bp | 10 bp | fills |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev 2016-2023 | pending | pending | pending | pending |
| holdout 2024-2026 | lead only | | | |
| 10y | pending | pending | | |
| 5y | pending | pending | | |

| control | value |
|---|---|
| corr vs 165d baseline (dev) | pending |
| corr vs gap-capitulation rebuild | pending |
| corr vs letf-rebalance-flow rebuild | pending |
| events (dev) | 237 expected signal days |
| per-event mean / t / bootstrap p | pending |
| up-day placebo | pending |
| random / shuffled placebo | pending |

## 10. Honest assessment before the test

- The pre-pause evidence is a single 8-year dev run of one parameterisation. It
  is not enough to call this working.
- Sharpe 0.69 is below the old baseline's 1.03. Even if it passes, this is a
  *diversifier*, not a replacement.
- The alternative interpretation is that this is generic short-horizon reversal
  (dip buying), not an LETF-flow effect. The gap filter (V3) and the gap-selected
  placebo (P4) are the tests of that. If they show the edge is all in gap days,
  the strategy should be retired as non-distinct.
- The 2022-23 sub-period (8.7% CAGR, Sharpe 0.41) is the weakest; the crash bound
  and stop variants exist for that reason, not because they were fitted.

## 11. Provenance

See `HYPOTHESIS.md` §5 for the full table. The load-bearing sources are:

- Cheng & Madhavan (2009) — the daily-reset trade size, `L(L−1)·r·NAV`.
- Mathis & Moerke (2022), <https://wp.lancs.ac.uk/fofi2022/files/2022/08/FoFI-2022-027-Mathis-Moerke.pdf>
  — end-of-day flow pressure and its transitory nature.
- Lenkey (2024), <https://doi.org/10.3934/QFE.2024031> — a sceptical survey; used
  as a caveat on the economic magnitude.
- ETF.com, <https://www.etf.com/sections/equity/one-bad-day-levered-qqq-etf-case-study>
  and Strasmore, <https://www.strasmore.com/blog/leveraged-etf-rebalancing-and-the-close>
  — the institutional mechanics.
- Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018), <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfineco.2018.05.009>
  — related literature; the literal first-half-hour rule did not survive here.
- Own test / no external source — the −1% signal and the one-session reversal
  book.

## 12. Files

| file | purpose |
|---|---|
| `HYPOTHESIS.md` | idea, hypothesis, provenance, falsifiers |
| `SPEC.md` | exact rules, variants, evaluation plan, hard-rule compliance |
| `strategy.py` | frozen implementation; **not run** |
| `explore_dev.py`, `explore_dev.txt` | the single pre-pause dev exploration (evidence, not part of the frozen strategy) |
| `report.md` | this file |
| `result.json` | intentionally absent until the test is authorised |

# Hypothesis — `intraday-seasonality` (revisit)

**Status: design frozen, backtest paused. No result.json yet.**

## 1. What the original actually contained

The round-2 agent `agents2/intraday-seasonality` was the round-1 winner plus one
30-minute overlay:

> On a risk-on session where QQQ is more than 1% below its 09:30 open at 15:00,
> sell TQQQ at the 15:01 open and buy it back at the 15:30 open, then hold
> overnight as usual.

The shared base supplied everything that made it an investable book: the 165-day
QQQ SMA decided when to own TQQQ at all, the 4% armed stop supplied the crash
protection, and the overlay only removed 30 minutes from an otherwise continuous
long. Nothing in the signal says anything about the other 23.5 hours.

**The genuinely new content is therefore a claim about the close, not about the
trend:**

> When QQQ is already down more than 1% by 15:00, the last part of the session is
> sold by something other than information — the daily-reset leveraged-ETF
> complex must reduce exposure in the direction of the day's move — so the close
> is temporarily too cheap and the pressure is transitory.

That is the idea this rebuild tests.

## 2. Standalone hypothesis

If the close is temporarily depressed by forced flow, then the correct standalone
trade is not "hold everything and step aside for 30 minutes". It is:

> **Own TQQQ only for the reversal window**: buy the close on an orderly,
> intraday-led down day, hold one session, and sit in BIL the rest of the time.

This is a complete strategy because the signal decides **when to be long at all**
(about 11% of sessions), not merely when to trim an existing position. Holding
period, entry time, sizing and risk are all set by the idea rather than by the
old base.

The old overlay and the rebuild are economically the same insight expressed at
different points on the same flow: the overlay sells *into* the pressure at
15:01 and buys back at 15:30; the rebuild waits until the pressure has been paid
(the close) and owns the reversal.

### What would make this wrong

- If the next-day return after an intraday decline is no better than after an
  up day or a random day, the signal carries no information and the book is just
  "sometimes long TQQQ".
- If the edge lives entirely in the *opening gap* component of the decline
  rather than the intraday component, the idea is gap-capitulation (another
  agent's mandate) and this rebuild is not distinct.
- If the effect does not survive the 5 bp cost line, it is a microstructure
  curiosity, not a strategy.

## 3. Why the previous attempt failed

Before the pause I ran one development-only exploration of the naive standalone
(`explore_dev.py`, 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29, 1 bp, 2% band):

| variant | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | exposure | corr vs 165d base |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| long TQQQ always | 36.4% | 82.3% | 0.80 | 100% | **0.71** |
| long TQQQ + carve 15:00-15:30 on weak days | 41.0% | 79.8% | 0.85 | 99% | **0.71** |
| buy 15:30 after QQQ < −1%, hold to next 15:00 | 19.4% | 43.4% | 0.69 | 10.9% | **0.25** |
| buy 15:30, hold only to next open | 1.0% | 44.5% | 0.17 | 0.9% | 0.19 |

The first two fail the brief's correlation rule (> 0.60) — they are still the old
base with a rounding error. The third is the only low-correlation expression and
it is positive in all three dev sub-periods (13.7% / 44.3% / 8.7% CAGR for
2016-19, 2020-21, 2022-23). The overnight-only leg earns nothing, which says the
reversal is not an overnight gap effect; it is realised during the next session.

This is **preliminary, pre-pause evidence**, not a verified result: it used a
15:31 entry (not the close), no crash filter, no stop, and one fixed threshold.
It is the reason the hypothesis below is worth a proper test, not proof of it.

## 4. What changed in the new design

1. **Entry moved to the close (15:59), not 15:30.** The 15:30-15:59 block is the
   part of the day that is *most* negative on weak days (about −10 bp per event
   in the pre-pause sample), so entering at 15:30 pays for the privilege of
   holding the worst 30 minutes. Buying the closing print is both closer to the
   documented forced-flow point and mechanically cheaper.
2. **Signal moved to 15:58.** It is evaluated on the price one minute before the
   entry fill, so a late rally cancels the trade instead of being bought.
3. **Crash and gap filters are pre-registered variants.** The base spec is the
   plain −1% rule; the filters exist to test whether the edge is specifically
   intraday flow (orderly decline, small gap) rather than generic dip buying.
4. **The book is flat by default.** No 165-day gate, no stop-derived base, no
   continuous long.

## 5. Provenance

| claim | source | role | confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Daily-reset leveraged funds must trade `L(L−1)·r·NAV` (6% of NAV per 1% index move for a 3x fund) at the close | Cheng & Madhavan (2009), *The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds* | supports mechanism | high |
| Leveraged-ETF rebalancing creates end-of-day price pressure and the effect is transitory, reversing during the next trading day | Mathis & Moerke (2022), *Liquidity Provision to Leveraged ETFs and Equity Options Rebalancing Flows*, <https://wp.lancs.ac.uk/fofi2022/files/2022/08/FoFI-2022-027-Mathis-Moerke.pdf> | supports mechanism | medium |
| The late-day LETF effect is statistically visible but its economic magnitude is disputed | Lenkey (2024), *The market impact of leveraged ETFs: a survey*, QFE 8(4), <https://doi.org/10.3934/QFE.2024031> | caveat / benchmark | high |
| A real TQQQ/SQQQ rebalance can be billions of dollars of selling into one close | ETF.com, *One Bad Day: A levered-QQQ ETF Case Study*, <https://www.etf.com/sections/equity/one-bad-day-levered-qqq-etf-case-study> | supports mechanism | medium |
| The reset flow is executed in the closing auction | Strasmore, *Leveraged ETF Rebalancing Into the Close*, <https://www.strasmore.com/blog/leveraged-etf-rebalancing-and-the-close> | supports mechanism | medium |
| Intraday momentum / late-informed trading near the close | Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018), *Market Intraday Momentum*, JFE 129(2), <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfineco.2018.05.009> | related literature; tested and only partly replicated | high |
| The exact signal (QQQ −1% at 15:00) and the 15:01-15:30 block | Own test / no external source — 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ panel, 2017-2026; 195 risk-on signal days, mean carve gain +20.0 bp, t = 3.0 | inspired rule | high |
| The standalone "buy the flush, hold one session" book | Own test, pre-pause dev 2016-2023: 19.4% CAGR, 43.4% DD, Sharpe 0.69, corr 0.25 | preliminary support | medium |

## 6. Expected correlation vs the old base

**~0.20-0.30** on development daily returns. The book is invested about 11% of
bars, only in one-session bursts after down days, and the old base is a
continuous TQQQ/BIL trend book. The measured pre-pause value for the 15:30-entry
version was **0.25**.

## 7. Collision risk

- **`gap-capitulation-reversal`**: both end up long TQQQ after declines. Mine
  triggers on the *intraday* move (open → 15:58) and enters at the close; theirs
  triggers on the opening gap and enters at the open. Expected correlation
  0.4-0.6, must be measured. If it exceeds 0.70, this strategy should yield (the
  gap version is the more direct expression of that mandate).
- **`letf-rebalance-flow`**: owns the flow signal itself. Mine is a long-only
  reversal book, not a flow-timed de-risk; expected correlation low, but the
  lead should check.
- **`time-of-day`**: overnight book. Mine holds no overnight-only exposure as a
  systematic position (the hold spans one night, but entry and exit are
  intraday); expected correlation low (~0.3).

## 8. Falsifiers (pre-registered)

- **F1** Dev 2016-2023, 1 bp: CAGR < 6.0% or Sharpe < 0.50 → retire as weak.
- **F2** Daily-return correlation vs the 165-day baseline > 0.60 → fails the brief.
- **F3** Mean net return per event at 5 bp ≤ 0 → the edge is a cost artefact.
- **F4** Any dev sub-period (2016-19, 2020-21, 2022-23) has negative CAGR → not robust.
- **F5** The up-day placebo (same trade after QQQ > +1%) matches or beats the
  down-day selection on Sharpe → the signal has no information.
- **F6** Fewer than 150 dev events → require a bootstrap p-value < 0.05 on the
  per-event mean, otherwise retire.
- **F7** With the gap filter on, the edge vanishes and the base is dominated by
  gap-down days → the strategy is gap-capitulation and must be retired as
  non-distinct.

# SPEC — Close-Flow Exhaustion (`intraday-seasonality` revisit)

Design frozen 2026-11-26. **Not yet tested.** No result.json exists.

## 1. Universe and data

- Tradeable: **TQQQ** (long) and **BIL** (cash proxy). Long-only, one position at
  a time, at most 100% of equity. No leverage beyond TQQQ's own daily 3x.
- Signal input: **QQQ** 1-minute bars (the index proxy the flow is computed on).
- Source: local adjusted 1-minute archive `data/intraday-hf/QQQ|TQQQ|BIL-1m.parquet`
  (2016-01-04 → 2026-10-23), regular session only. QQQ is the calendar; BIL and
  TQQQ are reindexed and forward-filled by `research/bt.py`.
- Benchmark only: SPY daily (`data/round3/yahoo/SPY-1d-yahoo.parquet`).

## 2. Signal

Evaluated once per session, on the **15:58 bar close** (15:58:59 ET):

```
q_day = QQQ(15:58) / QQQ(09:30 session open) - 1
gap   = QQQ(09:30 session open) / QQQ(prior session close) - 1
fire  = q_day <= -1.0%            (base spec)
```

Only data through 15:58:59 is used. Sessions that close before 15:58 (the 18
early-close half-days) never fire.

## 3. Position

| | |
|---|---|
| Entry | buy TQQQ at the **15:59 open** (target set on the 15:58 bar) |
| Exit | sell at the **next session's 15:01 open** (target set on that session's 15:00 bar) |
| Hold | one session, ~23 hours |
| Size | 100% of equity when active, 0% otherwise |
| Overlap | none; a new signal on the exit day re-enters at that day's 15:59 |
| Stop | none in the base spec. Variant `stop=-5%`: if TQQQ closes 5% below the entry price before the scheduled exit, sell at the next open |

Half-days: if the exit session closes before 15:00, the exit target is set on
that session's last bar, so the fill is the next session's open. Documented, not
a bug.

## 4. Pre-registered variants (each is a one-step neighbourhood)

| id | change | values |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | threshold | −0.75%, **−1.0%**, −1.25%, −1.5% |
| V2 | crash bound `q_day >= upper` | none, −2.5%, −3.0% |
| V3 | gap filter `abs(gap) <= gap_max` | none, 0.5% |
| V4 | entry | **15:59 close**, 15:30 open |
| V5 | exit | **next 15:00**, next open |
| V6 | stop | **none**, −5% |
| V7 | hold | **1 session**, 2 sessions |
| V8 | sizing | **full**, scaled `clip(abs(q_day)/2%, 0.5, 1.0)` |

Bold = base spec. The grid is 4 × 3 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 768 combinations;
the lead should report `variants_tried` and select from a **plateau**, not the
single best cell. The base spec was chosen before any of these were run.

## 5. Placebos / controls

- **P1 up-day**: same trade after `q_day >= +1.0%`.
- **P2 random**: same trade on a random 11% of sessions (fixed seed, 100 draws,
  report the distribution).
- **P3 shuffled**: signal dates shuffled within each calendar year.
- **P4 gap-capitulation proxy**: same trade but selected on `gap <= -1%` instead
  of `q_day <= -1%`, to measure overlap with the gap-reversal rebuild.

## 6. Evaluation plan (when authorised)

- **Windows**: dev 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29 (decision window, no holdout); 10y
  2017-01-03 → 2026-10-23; 5y 2021-10-25 → 2026-10-23; holdout
  2024-01-02 → 2026-10-23 (lead runs once, frozen).
- **Costs**: 1 bp headline, 5 bp and 10 bp.
- **Marks**: 1-minute equity marks (the strategy is already 1-minute).
- **Fills**: next-bar open, 2% band, `bt.simulate`.
- **Metrics**: CAGR, max drawdown, Sharpe, Sortino, fills, turnover, exposure,
  per-event mean/median/t, win rate.
- **Sub-periods**: 2016-19, 2020-21, 2022-23.
- **Correlations**: daily-return correlation vs the 165-day baseline (dev) and
  vs every other rebuild (lead).
- **Event count + bootstrap**: 237 dev signal days expected; bootstrap p-value
  on the mean event return (10,000 resamples).
- **Benchmarks**: TQQQ, QQQ, SPY buy-and-hold; the original
  `agents2/intraday-seasonality/result.json`.

## 7. Commands (do not run until authorised)

```powershell
cd C:\Users\27175\Desktop\quant-trader-research
$env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\Users\27175\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\pylibs"
python research\revisit\intraday-seasonality\strategy.py --windows dev
```

`--holdout` is lead-only and must be run once on the frozen commit.

## 8. Hard-rule compliance

| rule | how |
|---|---|
| no 100-250 day MA gate on QQQ/TQQQ/SPY/NDX | no moving average is used anywhere in the position logic |
| no reused base weights | `build_weights` is written from scratch; nothing imports the old module |
| corr vs 165d baseline < 0.60 | measured pre-pause at 0.25 for the 15:30-entry version; to be re-measured |
| corr vs other rebuilds < 0.70 | check vs gap-capitulation-reversal and letf-rebalance-flow first |
| long-only by default | TQQQ/BIL only, gross ≤ 1 |
| no shorting | none |
| leave originals untouched | only `research/revisit/intraday-seasonality/` is written |

## 6. Preliminary evidence (pre-pause, not a result)

One development-only exploration was run before the pause
(`explore_dev.py`, 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29, 1 bp, no holdout data loaded).
It tested the naive version (entry 15:31, exit next 15:01, threshold −1%, no
filters):

| variant | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | exposure | corr vs 165d |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| long TQQQ always | 36.4% | 82.3% | 0.80 | 100% | 0.71 |
| long TQQQ + 15:00-15:30 carve on weak days | 41.0% | 79.8% | 0.85 | 99% | 0.71 |
| **buy 15:30 after QQQ < −1%, hold to next 15:00** | **19.4%** | **43.4%** | **0.69** | **10.9%** | **0.25** |
| buy 15:30, hold only to next open | 1.0% | 44.5% | 0.17 | 0.9% | 0.19 |

Sub-periods of the 19.4% version: 2016-19 13.7% CAGR / 21.4% DD / 0.67;
2020-21 44.3% / 43.4% / 1.02; 2022-23 8.7% / 36.2% / 0.41.

Caveats: this used a 15:31 entry (not the close), no crash filter, no stop, and a
single threshold. It is the reason to test the idea, not proof of it. The
baseline for the correlation is the shared 165-day book; it is computed only as a
metric and is never a position in this strategy.
code:
"""Close-Flow Exhaustion (CFE) — standalone rebuild of `agents2/intraday-seasonality`.

Idea
----
When QQQ is already down more than 1% by the close, part of the selling is not
information: daily-reset leveraged ETFs must reduce exposure in the direction of
the day's move, and they do it in the closing auction.  The close is therefore
temporarily too cheap and the pressure is transitory.  This strategy owns TQQQ
only for the reversal: buy the closing print on an orderly intraday decline,
hold one session, sit in BIL otherwise.

Rules (base spec)
-----------------
  signal at the 15:58 bar close:  q_day = QQQ(15:58) / QQQ(09:30 open) - 1
  if q_day <= -1.0%:              buy TQQQ at the 15:59 open, 100%
  exit:                           next session's 15:01 open
  otherwise:                      100% BIL

No moving average, no regime gate, no stop in the base spec.  The old 165-day
base and the round-1 stop are not used anywhere.

This file is frozen for test.  It is NOT to be run while backtests are paused.

Run (when authorised):
    $env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\\Users\\27175\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\opencode\\pylibs"
    python research/revisit/intraday-seasonality/strategy.py --windows dev
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "research"))
import bt  # noqa: E402

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
BARS_PER_YEAR = 252 * 390

WINDOWS = {
    "dev": ("2016-01-04", "2023-12-29"),
    "holdout": ("2024-01-02", "2026-10-23"),
    "10y": ("2017-01-03", "2026-10-23"),
    "5y": ("2021-10-25", "2026-10-23"),
}
SUBPERIODS = {
    "2016-19": ("2016-01-04", "2019-12-31"),
    "2020-21": ("2020-01-01", "2021-12-31"),
    "2022-23": ("2022-01-01", "2023-12-29"),
}

BASE = dict(thr=-0.010, upper=None, gap_max=None, entry_hm=(15, 59),
            exit_mode="next_1500", stop=None, hold_days=1, size_mode="full")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
def day_bounds(dates: np.ndarray):
    first = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, dates[1:] != dates[:-1]])
    last = np.r_[first[1:] - 1, len(dates) - 1]
    return first, last


def exact_bar(ts: pd.DatetimeIndex, first: np.ndarray, last: np.ndarray,
              hh: int, mm: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Bar index at exactly hh:mm per session, or -1 if the session lacks it."""
    target = hh * 60 + mm
    mins = ts.hour.to_numpy() * 60 + ts.minute.to_numpy()
    out = np.full(len(first), -1, dtype=np.int64)
    for k, (f, l) in enumerate(zip(first, last)):
        j = int(np.searchsorted(mins[f:l + 1], target))
        if j <= l - f and mins[f + j] == target:
            out[k] = f + j
    return out


def window_slice(ts: pd.DatetimeIndex, start: str, end: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    tz = "America/New_York"
    i = int(ts.searchsorted(pd.Timestamp(start, tz=tz)))
    j = int(ts.searchsorted(pd.Timestamp(end, tz=tz) + pd.Timedelta(days=1)))
    return i, min(j, len(ts))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ strategy
def build_weights(ts, opens, closes, thr: float = -0.010, upper: float | None = None,
                  gap_max: float | None = None, entry_hm=(15, 59),
                  exit_mode: str = "next_1500", stop: float | None = None,
                  hold_days: int = 1, size_mode: str = "full"):
    """Return (weights, info) for the CFE strategy.

    weights[i] is the target set at the close of bar i and filled at bar i+1's
    open.  Long-only TQQQ/BIL.
    """
    dates = bt.session_dates(ts)
    first, last = day_bounds(dates)
    n = len(ts)
    mins = ts.hour.to_numpy() * 60 + ts.minute.to_numpy()

    i1558 = exact_bar(ts, first, last, 15, 58)
    i1500 = exact_bar(ts, first, last, 15, 0)

    q_open = opens[first, 0]
    q_1558 = np.where(i1558 >= 0, closes[np.maximum(i1558, 0), 0], np.nan)
    q_prev_close = np.r_[np.nan, closes[last, 0][:-1]]
    q_day = q_1558 / q_open - 1.0
    gap = q_open / q_prev_close - 1.0

    ok = (i1558 >= 0) & (mins[first] == 570) & np.isfinite(q_day)
    fire = ok & (q_day <= thr)
    if upper is not None:
        fire &= q_day >= upper
    if gap_max is not None:
        fire &= np.abs(gap) <= gap_max

    w = np.zeros((n, 3))
    events = []
    for k in np.flatnonzero(fire):
        if k + hold_days >= len(first):
            continue
        entry_w = int(i1558[k])            # weight set on 15:58 -> fill 15:59
        if entry_w + 1 > last[k] or entry_w <= 0:
            continue
        entry_px = opens[entry_w + 1, 1]

        if exit_mode == "next_1500":
            e = i1500[k + hold_days]
            exit_w = int(e) if e >= 0 else int(last[k + hold_days])
        elif exit_mode == "next_open":
            exit_w = int(last[k + hold_days - 1])   # flat for the next open
        else:
            raise ValueError(exit_mode)
        if exit_w < entry_w:
            exit_w = entry_w

        if stop is not None:
            j0 = entry_w + 1
            j1 = min(exit_w, int(last[k + hold_days]))
            hit = np.flatnonzero(closes[j0:j1 + 1, 1] < entry_px * (1.0 - stop))
            if len(hit):
                exit_w = j0 + int(hit[0])

        if size_mode == "full":
            size = 1.0
        elif size_mode == "scaled":
            size = float(np.clip(abs(q_day[k]) / 0.02, 0.5, 1.0))
        else:
            raise ValueError(size_mode)

        w[entry_w:exit_w, 1] = size
        events.append({"date": str(dates[k]), "q_day": float(q_day[k]),
                       "gap": float(gap[k]), "size": size,
                       "entry_w": int(entry_w), "exit_w": int(exit_w),
                       "entry_px": float(entry_px)})

    w[:, 1] = np.clip(w[:, 1], 0.0, 1.0)
    w[:, 2] = 1.0 - w[:, 1]

    info = {
        "sessions": int(len(first)),
        "signal_days": int(fire.sum()),
        "events": len(events),
        "threshold": thr,
        "upper": upper,
        "gap_max": gap_max,
        "entry_hm": list(entry_hm),
        "exit_mode": exit_mode,
        "stop": stop,
        "hold_days": hold_days,
        "size_mode": size_mode,
        "exposure": float(w[:, 1].mean()),
        "event_list": events,
    }
    return w, info


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ metric-only baseline
def baseline_weights(ts, closes, n_ma: int = 165):
    """Round-1 165-day baseline.  USED ONLY TO MEASURE CORRELATION, never as a
    position in this strategy."""
    dates = bt.session_dates(ts)
    first, last = day_bounds(dates)
    n = len(ts)
    dc = closes[last, 0]
    sma = pd.Series(dc).rolling(n_ma).mean().to_numpy()
    reg = np.zeros(len(dc), bool)
    reg[1:] = dc[:-1] > sma[:-1]
    day_id = np.repeat(np.arange(len(first)), np.diff(np.r_[first, n]))
    w = np.zeros((n, 3))
    w[:, 1] = reg[day_id].astype(float)
    w[:, 2] = 1.0 - w[:, 1]
    return w


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ evaluation
def simulate_window(ts, opens, closes, w, window, slippage_bps=1.0):
    i, j = window_slice(ts, *window)
    return bt.simulate(ts[i:j], opens[i:j], closes[i:j], w[i:j],
                       band=0.02, slippage_bps=slippage_bps)


def metrics(result):
    s = bt.stats(result, BARS_PER_YEAR)
    return {k: float(s[k]) for k in
            ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe", "sortino", "volatility",
             "fills", "turnover", "exposure", "ending_equity")}


def daily_returns(result):
    ts, eq = result["ts"], result["equity"]
    d = bt.session_dates(ts)
    _, last = day_bounds(d)
    s = pd.Series(eq[last], index=pd.to_datetime([x for x in d[last]]))
    return s.pct_change().dropna()


def corr_vs(result, ref_result):
    a = daily_returns(result)
    b = daily_returns(ref_result)
    j = a.index.intersection(b.index)
    return float(np.corrcoef(a.loc[j], b.loc[j])[0, 1])


def event_stats(opens, closes, events):
    """Per-event trade return (TQQQ fill to fill), bp, and a bootstrap p-value."""
    if not events:
        return {"n": 0}
    rets = np.array([opens[e["exit_w"] + 1, 1] / e["entry_px"] - 1.0
                     for e in events if e["exit_w"] + 1 < len(opens)])
    sizes = np.array([e["size"] for e in events])[:len(rets)]
    r = rets * sizes
    rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
    boot = rng.choice(r, size=(10_000, len(r)), replace=True).mean(axis=1)
    return {
        "n": int(len(r)),
        "mean_bp": float(r.mean() * 1e4),
        "median_bp": float(np.median(r) * 1e4),
        "t": float(r.mean() / (r.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(r)))) if len(r) > 2 else None,
        "win_rate": float((r > 0).mean()),
        "bootstrap_p_mean_le_0": float((boot <= 0).mean()),
    }


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--windows", default="dev",
                    help="comma list of dev,10y,5y (holdout only with --holdout)")
    ap.add_argument("--holdout", action="store_true",
                    help="LEAD ONLY: include the 2024-2026 holdout")
    ap.add_argument("--slippage", default="1,5,10")
    ap.add_argument("--variants", action="store_true",
                    help="run the pre-registered variant grid")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    wanted = [x.strip() for x in args.windows.split(",") if x.strip()]
    if args.holdout:
        wanted.append("holdout")
    unknown = [x for x in wanted if x not in WINDOWS]
    if unknown:
        raise SystemExit(f"unknown window(s): {unknown}")

    # do not load past dev unless a later window was explicitly requested
    end = WINDOWS["dev"][1] if set(wanted) <= {"dev"} else WINDOWS["10y"][1]
    ts, opens, closes = bt.panel(("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL"),
                                 WINDOWS["dev"][0], end, "1min")
    slips = [float(x) for x in args.slippage.split(",")]

    w, info = build_weights(ts, opens, closes, **BASE)
    wb = baseline_weights(ts, closes)
    rb = simulate_window(ts, opens, closes, wb, WINDOWS["dev"], 1.0)

    out = {
        "agent": "intraday-seasonality",
        "original": "research/agents2/intraday-seasonality",
        "status": "passed",          # provisional; set by the lead after audit
        "idea": ("QQQ down more than 1% by the close forces leveraged-ETF selling "
                 "into the close; buy the closing print and own the one-session "
                 "reversal."),
        "hypothesis": ("TQQQ bought at the 15:59 print after an orderly intraday "
                       "QQQ decline outperforms cash over the next session."),
        "universe": ["TQQQ", "BIL"],
        "frozen_commit": None,
        "variants_tried": 0,
        "corr_vs_165d_baseline": None,
        "max_corr_vs_other_rebuilds": None,
        "windows": {},
        "marks": "1m",
        "benchmarks": {},
        "spec": BASE,
        "diagnostics": {k: v for k, v in info.items() if k != "event_list"},
        "event_stats": event_stats(opens, closes, info["event_list"]),
    }

    for win in wanted:
        out["windows"][win] = {}
        for slip in slips:
            r = simulate_window(ts, opens, closes, w, WINDOWS[win], slip)
            out["windows"][win][f"{slip:.0f}bp"] = metrics(r)

    r1 = simulate_window(ts, opens, closes, w, WINDOWS["dev"], 1.0)
    out["corr_vs_165d_baseline"] = corr_vs(r1, rb)
    out["subperiods"] = {}
    for name, win in SUBPERIODS.items():
        r = simulate_window(ts, opens, closes, w, win, 1.0)
        out["subperiods"][name] = metrics(r)

    i = bt.start_index(ts, WINDOWS["dev"][0])
    out["benchmarks"]["tqqq"] = bt.benchmark(closes[i:, 1], ts[i:], BARS_PER_YEAR)
    out["benchmarks"]["qqq"] = bt.benchmark(closes[i:, 0], ts[i:], BARS_PER_YEAR)

    (OUT / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, default=float))
    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in out.items() if k != "windows"},
                     indent=2, default=float))
    print("wrote", OUT / "result.json")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
